segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod. My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 Englishpod。 我的名字是马可。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we're celebrating a very important and very special American holiday.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们正在庆祝一个非常重要且非常特别的美国假期。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we are celebrating and talking about Thanksgiving, a very, as you say, traditional and big holiday in the United States.
segments.zh: 今天我们正在庆祝和谈论感恩节，正如你所说，美国的传统和大节日。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this year it's on November 25th.
segments.zh: 所以今年是11月25日。

segments.en: It's always on a Thursday.
segments.zh: 它总是在星期四。

segments.en: Let's check out our dialogue to hear about what happens at this special dinner and why this is a holiday and then we'll be back to talk about it in just a moment.
segments.zh: 让我们看看我们的对话，了解在这顿特别的晚宴上会发生什么以及为什么这是一个假期，然后我们会在一瞬间回来谈论它。

segments.en: So, what are you doing for Thanksgiving?
segments.zh: 你感恩节有什么安排？

segments.en: Not much really.
segments.zh: 没什么特别安排。

segments.en: It's more of an American tradition. So back home we don't really celebrate it.
segments.zh: 这主要是美国的传统，我们老家不怎么过。

segments.en: In fact, I'm not even sure of what exactly is being celebrated.
segments.zh: 说真的，我连这个节日到底在庆祝什么都不太清楚。

segments.en: You know, it's a time to get together with all your family and be thankful for everything.
segments.zh: 这一天大家会和家人团聚，对拥有的一切心怀感恩。

segments.en: Yeah, but how did this holiday come to be?
segments.zh: 可这个节日是怎么来的？

segments.en: Well, the first settlers of Massachusetts arrived there because of religious persecution from England and King James.
segments.zh: 最早来到马萨诸塞的欧洲移民，是为了逃离英格兰詹姆斯国王时期的宗教迫害。

segments.en: Once in the New World, they befriended a native named Squanto who taught them how to harvest food from the area such as corn.
segments.zh: 来到新大陆后，他们结识了一位名叫斯宽托的原住民，他教他们种植和收获玉米等当地作物。

segments.en: And then what happened?
segments.zh: 然后发生了什么？

segments.en: Well, they had enough harvest for the next winter and in celebration they decided to have a big feast with the natives, giving thanks to the land and everyone for their food, health and new lives.
segments.zh: 收成足够他们度过接下来的冬天，于是他们决定和原住民一起举办盛宴，感谢这片土地和大家带来的食物、健康与新生活。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: I am amazed how big and delicious Thanksgiving dinners are.
segments.zh: 感恩节大餐那么丰盛又好吃，真让我惊讶。

segments.en: Come to my house for Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 来我家过感恩节。

segments.en: We're having turkey, pumpkin pie, mashed potatoes with gravy and lots of stuffing.
segments.zh: 有火鸡、南瓜派、浇了肉汁的土豆泥，还有满满的火鸡填料。

segments.en: Count me in!
segments.zh: 算我一个！

segments.en: All right, we're back. So a very interesting holiday.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了。 所以一个非常有趣的假期。

segments.en: We learned a little bit about why it's celebrated, how it came to be.
segments.zh: 我们了解了一些关于它为什么庆祝，它是如何诞生的。

segments.en: So let's take a look at some of those words now on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看现在关于语言外卖的一些词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway
segments.zh: 语言要点

segments.en: The first word we have for you guys today on Language Takeaway is settler.
segments.zh: 我们今天在语言外卖上给你们的第一个词是 Settler。

segments.en: Now, a settler is a person.
segments.zh: 现在，定居者是一个人。

segments.en: What kind of a person is a settler?
segments.zh: 什么样的人是定居者？

segments.en: Basically, it's a person that goes to a place to settle down there or to settle there and that basically means to live there, to stay there permanently.
segments.zh: 基本上，它是一个人去那里定居或在那里定居，这基本上意味着住在那里，永久地呆在那里。

segments.en: All right, but the idea with a settler is that he or she will start to build something, build a house, build a city, build a town.
segments.zh: 好吧，但与定居者的想法是，他或她将开始建造一些东西，建造房子，建造一座城市，建造一个城镇。

segments.en: So settlers go to places where there aren't very many people.
segments.zh: 所以定居者去人不多的地方。

segments.en: That's right. Kind of hard to be a settler now.
segments.zh: 没错。 现在很难成为定居者。

segments.en: But yeah, back then, obviously, there were so many places that were undiscovered or didn't have people and they would settle there.
segments.zh: 但是，是的，当时，很明显，有很多地方没有被发现或没有人，他们会在那里定居。

segments.en: And the place where they went in the United States is called Massachusetts.
segments.zh: 他们去美国的地方叫马萨诸塞州。

segments.en: Massachusetts. Now, this is a very long, very hard to pronounce word and I believe it comes from a local Indian language.
segments.zh: 马萨诸塞州。 现在，这是一个很长，很难发音的单词，我相信它来自当地的印度语言。

segments.en: But Massachusetts, if you break it down, Massachusetts is a state.
segments.zh: 但是马萨诸塞州，如果你把它分解，马萨诸塞州就是一个州。

segments.en: And you might have heard of the biggest city in Massachusetts, which is Boston.
segments.zh: 您可能听说过马萨诸塞州最大的城市，即波士顿。

segments.en: So Boston, Massachusetts. But this is where the settlers first came when they came to America.
segments.zh: 所以波士顿，马萨诸塞州。 但这就是定居者来到美国时第一次来到这里的地方。

segments.en: That's right. So I think if you go to Boston, it has kind of this atmosphere of the settlers and how this old little touch to it of how it used to be.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以我想如果你去波士顿，它有一种定居者的气氛，以及它过去的这种古老的小感触。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: There is an old feel to Boston because unlike most places in America, Boston has been a city for over 400 years, almost 500 years.
segments.zh: 波士顿有一种古老的感觉，因为与美国的大多数地方不同，波士顿已经有 400 多年的历史，将近 500 年。

segments.en: So it's much different from places like California or Texas.
segments.zh: 所以它与加利福尼亚或德克萨斯等地有很大不同。

segments.en: That's right. OK. So the settlers arrived to Massachusetts and they went there because of religious persecution from England and King James.
segments.zh: 没错。 好的。 于是定居者抵达马萨诸塞州，由于来自英格兰和詹姆斯国王的宗教迫害，他们去了那里。

segments.en: OK. So the key here is persecution.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以这里的关键是迫害。

segments.en: This is something that you do to someone else or this is something a government does to someone else.
segments.zh: 这是你对别人做的事情，或者这是政府对别人做的事情。

segments.en: Basically, to persecute someone is to is to limit them or to attack them or to to prevent them from doing things that they want to do.
segments.zh: 基本上，迫害某人就是限制他们或攻击他们或阻止他们做他们想做的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So basically, that is the reason why they left England, because the king was persecuting them.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，这就是他们离开英格兰的原因，因为国王正在迫害他们。

segments.en: They didn't let them be have their own religion.
segments.zh: 他们没有让他们有自己的宗教。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: They had this religion and the king did not approve of the religion and they felt like people were critical of them or attacking them or preventing them from practicing this religion.
segments.zh: 他们有这种宗教，国王不赞成宗教，他们觉得人们批评他们或攻击他们或阻止他们信奉这种宗教。

segments.en: And so their religious persecution in England pushed them to this place, the New World.
segments.zh: 因此，他们在英国的宗教迫害将他们推向了这个地方，即新世界。

segments.en: So that's our next word.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们的下一个词。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: The New World.
segments.zh: 新世界。

segments.en: And this is what they used to call the continent of United States or North America.
segments.zh: 这就是他们过去所说的美国或北美大陆。

segments.en: They used to call it the New World. All right.
segments.zh: 他们曾经称之为新世界。 好的。

segments.en: So New World, Old World.
segments.zh: 所以新世界，旧世界。

segments.en: So if we think of Europe as being the old world, America, like you're saying, Latin America, North America, these are part of the New World.
segments.zh: 因此，如果我们将欧洲视为旧世界，美国，就像您所说的拉丁美洲、北美洲，这些都是新世界的一部分。

segments.en: So it's almost like they had never been discovered before.
segments.zh: 所以这几乎就像他们以前从未被发现过一样。

segments.en: Right. So, yeah, basically everyone was concentrated in Europe at that time.
segments.zh: 对。 所以，是的，当时基本上每个人都集中在欧洲。

segments.en: And then when they went to the West, they went to the New World.
segments.zh: 然后当他们去西方时，他们去了新世界。

segments.en: And obviously, when they arrived, it wasn't empty.
segments.zh: 显然，当他们到达时，它不是空的。

segments.en: They had people there.
segments.zh: 他们在那里有人。

segments.en: And we say that they are the natives of that land.
segments.zh: 我们说他们是那片土地的当地人。

segments.en: OK, so a native of some place is someone who comes from there originally.
segments.zh: 好的，所以某个地方的本地人最初是来自那里的人。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So if I came to America in 1500, there were Native American Indians who were living there.
segments.zh: 因此，如果我在 1500 年来到美国，就会有美洲原住民印第安人住在那里。

segments.en: And so they're the natives of this place.
segments.zh: 所以他们是这个地方的本地人。

segments.en: Now, can you use that nowadays?
segments.zh: 现在，你现在可以使用它吗？

segments.en: Can you say I am a native of Italy?
segments.zh: 你能说我是意大利人吗？

segments.en: I'm a native of Italy.
segments.zh: 我是意大利人。

segments.en: I'm a native of Chicago.
segments.zh: 我是芝加哥人。

segments.en: Yes, you can.
segments.zh: 是的，你可以。

segments.en: It's a little bit, you know, it's a little bit less common than saying I'm from Chicago or I'm from Italy, but it's also correct.
segments.zh: 这有点，你知道，这比说我来自芝加哥或来自意大利要少一些，但这也是正确的。

segments.en: OK, but in this case, we're talking about the natives as the people who were already there.
segments.zh: 好的，但在这种情况下，我们谈论的是当地人作为已经在那里的人。

segments.en: Yes, Native American Indians. Like Squanto.
segments.zh: 是的，美洲原住民印第安人。 像斯普兰托。

segments.en: Like Squanto.
segments.zh: 像斯普兰托。

segments.en: That's the name of that Native American Indian who was there.
segments.zh: 那是那个在那里的美洲原住民印第安人的名字。

segments.en: And this native named Squanto taught them how to harvest food from the area such as corn.
segments.zh: 这个名叫 Squanto 的本地人教他们如何从玉米等地区收获食物。

segments.en: So this is the interesting part of the story.
segments.zh: 所以这是故事中有趣的部分。

segments.en: It is.
segments.zh: 确实很有意思。

segments.en: Basically, these two groups worked together.
segments.zh: 基本上，这两个小组一起工作。

segments.en: You have Native American Indians and settlers, and they worked together to make a meal and to survive, basically.
segments.zh: 你有美洲原住民印第安人和定居者，他们基本上一起做饭和生存。

segments.en: And to harvest food, to harvest, the key here is that it's a verb.
segments.zh: 为了收获食物，收获，这里的关键是它是一个动词。

segments.en: It's something you do to crops or like corn or potatoes.
segments.zh: 这是你对作物或玉米或土豆做的事情。

segments.en: And you take them out from the field and you bring them home.
segments.zh: 你把它们从田野里拿出来，然后把它们带回家。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So in this case, the corn is growing out of the land. And if you go out and cut it down and take it, you are harvesting corn.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，玉米正在从土地上生长出来。 如果你出去把它剪下来拿走它，你就是在收割玉米。

segments.en: You are you're picking it, collecting it.
segments.zh: 你是你在挑选它，收集它。

segments.en: Exactly. And so they harvested the food and they have a very big meal.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以他们收获了食物，他们吃了一顿大餐。

segments.en: So we do want to talk about the special meal here that features all of this harvested food.
segments.zh: 所以我们确实想在这里谈论以所有这些收获的食物为特色的特殊餐点。

segments.en: Let's take a look at some of those words in Language Takeaway Part 2.
segments.zh: 让我们来看看语言外卖第 2 部分中的一些单词。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So talking about the foods.
segments.zh: 所以说说食物。

segments.en: Now, obviously, the tradition is that you have this big meal together.
segments.zh: 现在，显然，传统是你们一起吃这顿大餐。

segments.en: And the one thing that is, I think, a given is that you have a big turkey.
segments.zh: 我认为，一件事是你有一只大火鸡。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a turkey is a bird.
segments.zh: 所以火鸡是一只鸟。

segments.en: They make very funny sounds, don't they?
segments.zh: 他们发出非常有趣的声音，不是吗？

segments.en: Right. Like gobble, gobble, gobble.
segments.zh: 对。 像狼吞虎咽，狼吞虎咽，狼吞虎咽。

segments.en: But they they're very big. They run around and they have this red part under their neck and beaks and everything.
segments.zh: 但他们非常大。 他们到处乱跑，脖子和喙下都有这个红色的部分。

segments.en: So it's a very commonly eaten food for Thanksgiving. But people can eat it anytime.
segments.zh: 所以它是感恩节非常普遍吃的食物。 但人们可以随时吃。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: This is a weird thing.
segments.zh: 这是一件奇怪的事情。

segments.en: I usually don't see turkey too much, if not during Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 如果不是在感恩节期间，我通常不会看太多火鸡。

segments.en: Like I don't see somebody like a restaurant offering turkey.
segments.zh: 就像我没有看到像一家提供火鸡的餐厅一样。

segments.en: No, you don't.
segments.zh: 不，你没有。

segments.en: But you do see it in delis like a roast turkey sandwich.
segments.zh: 但你确实在熟食店里看到它，就像烤火鸡三明治一样。

segments.en: Yes, this is true.
segments.zh: 是的，这是真的。

segments.en: Because turkey is very healthy.
segments.zh: 因为土耳其非常健康。

segments.en: OK. So we have turkey.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以我们有土耳其。

segments.en: We also have pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 我们还有南瓜派。

segments.en: So pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 所以南瓜派。

segments.en: Pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 南瓜饼。

segments.en: This is a classic.
segments.zh: 这是一个经典。

segments.en: You've heard of apple pie.
segments.zh: 你听说过苹果派。

segments.en: But pumpkin pie is a baked dessert that is filled with some pumpkin filling.
segments.zh: 但南瓜派是一种烤甜点，里面装满了一些南瓜馅。

segments.en: So as you know, pumpkin or may know pumpkin is a big...
segments.zh: 如你所知，南瓜或可能知道南瓜是一个大...

segments.en: It's a gourd.
segments.zh: 这是一个葫芦。

segments.en: It's a gourd.
segments.zh: 这是一个葫芦。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I think it's kind of vegetable.
segments.zh: 我认为这是一种蔬菜。

segments.en: Kind of like a vegetable.
segments.zh: 有点像蔬菜。

segments.en: It's big and orange.
segments.zh: 它又大又橙色。

segments.en: And basically this is a...
segments.zh: 基本上这是一个...

segments.en: It's kind of sweet, right? The insides.
segments.zh: 有点甜，对吧？ 内部。

segments.en: It is.
segments.zh: 是有点甜。

segments.en: It's a little bit sweet.
segments.zh: 这有点甜。

segments.en: It's big, orange and round, like you say.
segments.zh: 就像你说的，它很大，橙色和圆形。

segments.en: People often start to harvest them around October.
segments.zh: 人们经常在 10 月左右开始收获它们。

segments.en: I'd say.
segments.zh: 我会说。

segments.en: Some people like to eat the seeds.
segments.zh: 有些人喜欢吃种子。

segments.en: But you can also scoop out with your spoon.
segments.zh: 但你也可以用勺子舀出。

segments.en: You can take out some of the meat, some of the filling.
segments.zh: 你可以取出一些肉，一些馅料。

segments.en: And that's what we use to create this pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 这就是我们用来制作这个南瓜派的东西。

segments.en: Very good. So pumpkin pie.
segments.zh: 非常好。 所以南瓜派。

segments.en: Delicious food.
segments.zh: 美味的食物。

segments.en: Now we also have a typical mashed potatoes with gravy.
segments.zh: 现在我们也有一个典型的土豆泥和肉汁。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I love mashed potatoes.
segments.zh: 我喜欢土豆泥。

segments.en: Mashed means to squish or to break down or to push down.
segments.zh: 捣碎的意思是压扁或分解或向下推。

segments.en: And so mashed potatoes, you have a normal potato and you mix up all the potatoes together.
segments.zh: 所以土豆泥，你有一个普通的土豆，你把所有的土豆都混合在一起。

segments.en: So it's kind of like soft and creamy.
segments.zh: 所以它有点像柔软和奶油。

segments.en: Yeah. It almost becomes like a paste or almost like, let's say, like ice cream, but not cold.
segments.zh: 是的。 它几乎变成了糊状物，或者几乎就像冰淇淋一样，但不像冰淇淋。

segments.en: Not cold and not sweet.
segments.zh: 不冷也不甜。

segments.en: But yeah, that's the consistency.
segments.zh: 但是，是的，这就是一致性。

segments.en: That's what it feels like.
segments.zh: 这就是它的感觉。

segments.en: And so when we eat potatoes like this, in America, we often like to eat it with a sauce.
segments.zh: 所以当我们像这样吃土豆时，在美国，我们经常喜欢用酱汁吃它。

segments.en: And the sauce that we eat with mashed potatoes is called gravy.
segments.zh: 我们和土豆泥一起吃的酱汁被称为肉汁。

segments.en: Gravy. And now gravy is usually made out of what?
segments.zh: 肉汁。 而现在肉汁通常是用什么做的？

segments.en: Gravy is made from...
segments.zh: 肉汁是用...

segments.en: Well, you can make different kinds of gravy.
segments.zh: 好吧，你可以做不同种类的肉汁。

segments.en: But the way that we make it at my house is we take all of the juice from the turkey.
segments.zh: 但我们在我家做的方式是我们从火鸡中取出所有的果汁。

segments.en: Because when you bake a turkey in the oven, on the bottom of the pan you'll get some liquid, some water, some fat.
segments.zh: 因为当你在烤箱里烤火鸡时，在平底锅的底部你会得到一些液体，一些水，一些脂肪。

segments.en: And you use that to make a gravy.
segments.zh: 你用它来做肉汁。

segments.en: So it's brown and it's very salty and delicious.
segments.zh: 所以它是棕色的，非常咸和美味。

segments.en: Awesome.
segments.zh: 太棒了。

segments.en: Sounds delicious. And to end things, we have stuffing.
segments.zh: 听起来很好吃。 为了结束事情，我们有填充物。

segments.en: Now this stuffing goes inside the turkey, right?
segments.zh: 现在这种馅料进入火鸡，对吧？

segments.en: But then you take it out.
segments.zh: 但是你把它拿出来。

segments.en: That's right. So stuffing, we talk about stuffing in general as being something that you put inside something else.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以填充，我们一般来说填充填充是你放在其他东西中的东西。

segments.en: So if I have a stuffed animal, he has some cotton inside or whatever.
segments.zh: 所以如果我有一个毛绒玩具，他里面有一些棉花或其他什么。

segments.en: But if you have a turkey, you take out all of the organs, the heart, the liver.
segments.zh: 但如果你有一只火鸡，你会拿出所有的器官，心脏，肝脏。

segments.en: You take those parts out because we don't eat those.
segments.zh: 你把那些部分拿出来，因为我们不吃那些。

segments.en: And you put some bread, onions and vegetables inside the turkey to cook.
segments.zh: 你在火鸡里放了一些面包、洋葱和蔬菜来做饭。

segments.en: And then you take it out and you eat it.
segments.zh: 然后你把它拿出来，你吃掉它。

segments.en: So it tastes a bit like turkey and meat, but it's very delicious.
segments.zh: 所以它的味道有点像火鸡和肉，但它非常美味。

segments.en: But you eat it apart, kind of like let's say rice.
segments.zh: 但是你把它分开吃，有点像米饭。

segments.en: Like a side dish.
segments.zh: 像一道菜。

segments.en: Like a side dish.
segments.zh: 像一道菜。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: It sounds delicious.
segments.zh: 听起来很好吃。

segments.en: And obviously it's a very big meal, but very, very common, a traditional holiday in the United States.
segments.zh: 显然这是一顿非常大的饭菜，但非常非常常见，是美国的传统假期。

segments.en: It's very fun to celebrate as well. You get together with family and you have this nice meal together.
segments.zh: 庆祝也很有趣。 你和家人在一起，你们一起吃这顿美餐。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It's a wonderful holiday.
segments.zh: 这是一个美妙的假期。

segments.en: And we'll be talking a bit about it in a second.
segments.zh: 我们稍后会谈谈它。

segments.en: But let's just take one more listen to today's dialogue.
segments.zh: 但是，让我们再听一听今天的对话。

segments.en: So what are you doing for Thanksgiving?
segments.zh: 那么感恩节你在做什么呢？

segments.en: Not much, really.
segments.zh: 不多，真的。

segments.en: It's more of an American tradition. So back home, we don't really celebrate it.
segments.zh: 这更像是美国的传统。 所以回到家里，我们并没有真正庆祝它。

segments.en: In fact, I'm not even sure of what exactly is being celebrated.
segments.zh: 说真的，我连这个节日到底在庆祝什么都不太清楚。

segments.en: Well, you know, it's a time to get together with all your family and be thankful for everything.
segments.zh: 好吧，你知道，现在是与全家人团聚并感谢一切的时候了。

segments.en: Yeah, but how did this holiday come to be?
segments.zh: 可这个节日是怎么来的？

segments.en: Well, the first settlers of Massachusetts arrived there because of religious persecution from England and King James.
segments.zh: 最早来到马萨诸塞的欧洲移民，是为了逃离英格兰詹姆斯国王时期的宗教迫害。

segments.en: Once in the New World, they befriended a native named Squanto who taught them how to harvest food from the area, such as corn.
segments.zh: 一旦进入新大陆，他们就结识了一位名叫 Squanto 的本地人，他教他们如何从该地区（例如玉米）收获食物。

segments.en: And then what happened?
segments.zh: 然后发生了什么？

segments.en: Well, they had enough harvest for the next winter, and in celebration, they decided to have a big feast with the natives, giving thanks to the land and everyone for their food, health and new lives.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们为明年的冬天收获了足够的收成，为了庆祝，他们决定与当地人一起举行盛大的盛宴，感谢土地和每个人的食物、健康和新生活。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: I am amazed how big and delicious Thanksgiving dinners are.
segments.zh: 感恩节大餐那么丰盛又好吃，真让我惊讶。

segments.en: Come to my house for Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 来我家过感恩节。

segments.en: We're having turkey, pumpkin pie, mashed potatoes with gravy and lots of stuffing.
segments.zh: 有火鸡、南瓜派、浇了肉汁的土豆泥，还有满满的火鸡填料。

segments.en: Count me in.
segments.zh: 算我一个。

segments.en: All right, so Thanksgiving is a national holiday.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以感恩节是一个国定假日。

segments.en: Now, is it you said it's a Thursday.
segments.zh: 现在，是你说是星期四吗？

segments.en: It's always on Thursday.
segments.zh: 总是在星期四。

segments.en: So you get that Thursday off from school, from work and everything.
segments.zh: 所以你在星期四放学，下班和一切。

segments.en: You get Thursday and Friday.
segments.zh: 你得到星期四和星期五。

segments.en: So you get two days.
segments.zh: 所以你有两天。

segments.en: Yeah, it's a four day weekend.
segments.zh: 是的，这是一个四天的周末。

segments.en: Oh, nice.
segments.zh: 哦，真不错。

segments.en: And it's a wonderful holiday because it's something that everybody in America can celebrate.
segments.zh: 这是一个美好的假期，因为这是美国每个人都可以庆祝的事情。

segments.en: Because, you know, for Christmas, for example, some people don't celebrate Christmas.
segments.zh: 因为，你知道，例如，在圣诞节，有些人不庆祝圣诞节。

segments.en: Or you don't really get holiday time off during the summer for everyone, maybe just the schoolchildren.
segments.zh: 或者你并没有真正为每个人在暑假休假，也许只是学童。

segments.en: And so this is actually a nice holiday because everybody is home.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上是一个不错的假期，因为每个人都在家。

segments.en: Right. So it doesn't have a religious connotation because you're talking about, you know, the settlers and how they arrived there and they survived a harsh winter.
segments.zh: 对。 所以它没有宗教内涵，因为你在谈论定居者以及他们如何到达那里，他们在严酷的冬天中幸存下来。

segments.en: And so, as you say, it's kind of like a neutral holiday where you just it's a good excuse to get together, have a big meal and just spend quality time with the family.
segments.zh: 所以，正如你所说，这有点像一个中立的假期，你只是一个聚在一起的好借口，吃一顿大餐，和家人共度美好时光。

segments.en: That's right. You cook all day.
segments.zh: 没错。 你做饭一整天。

segments.en: You eat.
segments.zh: 你吃。

segments.en: You watch some football on TV.
segments.zh: 你在电视上看一些足球。

segments.en: You spend some time with your family and you fall asleep very, very full.
segments.zh: 你花了一些时间和家人在一起，你睡得非常非常饱。

segments.en: So this is another very interesting thing is that usually on TV, because everyone is home, everyone is having dinner or spending time with each other, they will have a football game on TV for Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一个非常有趣的事情，通常在电视上，因为每个人都在家，每个人都在吃饭或互相花时间，他们将在电视上有一场足球比赛过感恩节。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So everyone's sitting around eating dinner and then there's a football game on the TV.
segments.zh: 所以每个人都坐在旁边吃晚饭，然后电视上有一场足球比赛。

segments.en: Wow. So that kind of that's kind of bad for the football players that have to be playing on Thanksgiving Day.
segments.zh: 哇。 所以这对那些必须在感恩节踢球的足球运动员来说是不利的。

segments.en: Yeah, but they get all hungry, you know, out there on the field and they get to go home and eat a big turkey.
segments.zh: 是的，但他们都饿了，你知道，在球场上，他们可以回家吃一只大火鸡。

segments.en: And have a big meal.
segments.zh: 并吃一顿大餐。

segments.en: It's very, very interesting.
segments.zh: 这非常非常有趣。

segments.en: We'll put some pictures of the food that is commonly served on this holiday.
segments.zh: 我们将在这个假期提供一些食物的照片。

segments.en: And it would be interesting to know if I know a lot of our listeners are not originally from the United States.
segments.zh: 如果我知道我们的很多听众不是来自美国，那会很有趣。

segments.en: So if you are there, tell us if you've celebrated it or how have you seen it or will you celebrate it or any story that you can share with us.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您在那里，请告诉我们您是否庆祝过它，或者您是如何看到它的，或者您会庆祝它或您可以与我们分享的任何故事。

segments.en: That's right. We are very excited to hear this from you and we wish you all a very happy Thanksgiving.
segments.zh: 没错。 我们很高兴听到您的消息，我们祝大家感恩节快乐。

segments.en: Visit our site EnglishPod.com to tell us more.
segments.zh: 访问我们的网站 englishpod.com 告诉我们更多。

segments.en: All right. We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好的。 我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
